definitions.explanation: The movement or operation of a vehicle along a road or track. Used almost exclusively for vehicles, not for people running on foot.

examples.japanese: {走行|そうこう}{距離|きょり}を{確認|かくにん}する。
{高速|こうそく}{道路|どうろ}を{時速|じそく}100キロで{走行|そうこう}する。
examples.english: To drive at 100 km/h on the expressway.

examples.japanese: この{車|くるま}は{走行|そうこう}{距離|きょり}が10{万|まん}キロを{超|こ}えているが、まだまだ{元気|げんき}に{走|はし}る。
examples.english: This car has over 100,000 kilometers on it, but it still runs well.

notes:
{走行|そうこう} refers specifically to the movement of vehicles, not people. It is commonly seen on car dashboards, in driving manuals, and in traffic-related contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {走行|そうこう}{距離|きょり} (mileage, distance traveled)
- {走行|そうこう}{中|ちゅう} (while driving/in motion)
- {走行|そうこう}{速度|そくど} (driving speed)
- {走行|そうこう}{車線|しゃせん} (driving lane)
- {自動|じどう}{走行|そうこう} (autonomous driving)

WHEN NOT USED:
{走行|そうこう} is not used for people running on foot. Use {走|はし}る or ランニング for that.
